pk.context: 5 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Turnover of its enzyme complex takes about 30 days, setting this 5-alpha reductase inhibitor apart from others.

clues.text: Bioavailability averages 63% and is not affected by food. About 90% is bound to plasma proteins, and it is extensively metabolized in the liver, mainly by CYP3A4, with 57% of the dose excreted in feces.
Molecular weight 372.5. A white crystalline powder with a melting point near 250°C, practically insoluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 5 mg tablets, with a recommended dose of 5 mg a day.

No boxed warning. Contraindicated in pregnancy and hypersensitivity to any component; it may cause abnormal external genitalia in a male fetus, and the most common reactions relate to sexual function.
Symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia in men with an enlarged prostate, to improve symptoms and reduce acute urinary retention.
A competitive, specific inhibitor of type II 5α-reductase, the enzyme that converts testosterone to DHT, with no affinity for androgen receptors.
The generic name begins with F and has eleven letters.
